title: Capstone: Support-Agent Harness
objective: After this lesson you will be able to assemble the complete support-agent harness (budgets, memory, registry, loops, errors, traces, guards, gold) from the course's pieces, evaluate it with attribution, and present it as traced runs plus a findings memo — ready for the final assessment and your capstone project.
why: Nine lessons of scaffolding pieces; one lesson of assembled system. The walkthrough builds the harness once — budgeted context, policy memory, versioned tools, terminating loops, classified errors, replayable traces, enforced guardrails, gated gold — so your project repeats a demonstrated shape with numbers attached. Assembly is the final harness skill.

blocks.text: Build in dependency order with verification per piece: (1) **budgets + registry** (context fits longest gold; tools versioned); (2) **memory policies** (write/decay/retrieve proven); (3) **loops + errors** (termination + classification tested); (4) **traces + guards** (replay deterministic, attack gold passing); (5) **gold eval** (baseline + one iteration with attribution). No piece starts on unverified prior output — dependency order with proof.

blocks.caption: Manifest-first: gates per piece, numbers per claim

blocks.text: Three traced runs (the demo that proves)

Happy (late parcel → answered with citations, 3 steps), edge (vague multi-issue → clarified → resolved), attack (injection → quarantined pre-tool with logged attempt). Each with trace (spans + verdicts), memory reads/writes shown, guardrail verdicts attached. Demos without traces are theater; with per-piece evidence, proof.

Baseline per component with weakest named, one iterated fix with delta (memory retrieval tuning after misses), budget headroom statement, decay schedule, deprecation calendar, and deferred list (semantic caching next, multi-agent later). Measured, cited, improvable — the deliverable stakeholders fund and operators run.

blocks.title: Audit the manifest
blocks.note: Run it: expect eight PASS lines then 'manifest sound'. Piecewise gates audited before a single conversation runs — manifest-first means machine-checkable harnesses.

items: Assemble in dependency order with per-piece gates: budgets → memory → registry → loops/errors → traces/guards → eval
Trace one run per kind (happy/edge/attack) with piece-level evidence; memo findings per component
Deferred list with reasons; budgets/schedules/calendars as living operations docs

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the manifest audit and confirm soundness. (b) Break it (attack gold 7/9) and state the review outcome + required fix. (c) Draft your capstone manifest (same shape, your domain's pieces) with one measured-or-contracted entry per piece.
hints: Baseline sound (8 PASS); broken guards fail the manifest → assembly halts until 9/9 (gates gate).
7/9 attack gold means two bypass shapes unhandled: add rules + gold pins, re-run to full coverage.
Your manifest needs per-piece entries with numbers-or-contracts: budgets, policies, versions, terminations, classes, determinism, gold.
exercise.why: Gate-driven assembly (failed gates halt downstream) plus manifest auditing makes harness construction verifiable at every arrow — practiced on breakage, not just success.
exercise.code: // Manifest-audit pattern: per-piece requirements as runnable checks.

options: Budgets → memory → registry → loops/errors → traces/guards → eval — dependencies first, verified per piece
quiz.explain: Dependency order with per-piece gates: each layer builds on verified prior output. Budgets and registries precede the loops that consume them.

quiz.q: Attack gold at 7/9 during assembly. Proceed?
options: No: gate fails → fix rules + pin gold to full coverage first; unhandled bypass shapes ship as incidents
quiz.explain: Gates gate assembly, not just merges: 2 unhandled bypasses are 2 future incidents with known shapes. Fix, pin, re-audit.

options: Machine-checkable architecture: per-piece requirements audited before runs — coverage thinking for builds
quiz.explain: Manifests convert architecture opinions into runnable checks. Reviewers verify gates, not prose — coverage thinking extends to builds.

summary: Manifest-audited assembly, one traced run per kind with piece evidence, findings per component, deferred list with reasons. Nine lessons become one operating harness — assessment next, capstone after.
next: Course complete: take the 12-question final assessment (70% to pass), then ship the Support-Agent Harness capstone — and step into Spring AI.
